settings.discordBridgeIsActiveHint: When disabled, stops sending signals to and from relays. Basically disables the module's functionality
settings.overlayPopup: Open the Overlay in a separate window
settings.overlayPopupHint: Determines whether the Overlay (StreamKit) opens in a separate window or in a new browser tab
settings.speakingEventDebounceMsHint: "Started speaking" is only sent if the person speaks longer than this — so short sounds (coughs, clicks) don't trigger highlights or macros. The cost: the start of every phrase is detected with this delay. 0 disables the filter. Applies to all players
settings.speakingStopDelayMsHint: "Stopped speaking" is only sent if the person doesn't speak again within this time — so short pauses inside a phrase don't turn off highlights or trigger macros twice. The cost: the end of every phrase is detected with this delay. 0 disables the delay. Applies to all players
settings.allowPlayerRules: Allow players to create macro rules
settings.allowPlayerRulesHint: Players can assign their own macros to Discord events. Player rules run only for that player and with their permissions

relayStatusHint.STARTING: the relay is running but not working yet

IDLE.title: Nobody is relaying
IDLE.text: Nobody is running the relay right now. Press "Enable relay" to become the relay
IDLE.textActive: You can enable the relay too — you'll become a backup and take over if the primary relay disconnects

APP.title: FoundryVTT desktop app detected
APP.text: The relay only works in a browser: TamperMonkey scripts don't run in the FoundryVTT desktop app. Copy the world link, open it in a browser with TamperMonkey installed and enable the relay there

DISABLED.title: Module disabled
DISABLED.text: Discord Relay is disabled in the module settings. The GM can enable it

NO_CHANNEL.title: No voice channel set
NO_CHANNEL.text: The GM must enter a Discord voice channel link in the field below

POPUP_BLOCKED.title: Window blocked by the browser
POPUP_BLOCKED.text: The browser blocked the StreamKit window. Allow pop-ups for this site (usually an icon in the address bar) and press the button again

CONNECTING.title: Connecting…
CONNECTING.text: The StreamKit window is open, waiting for the TamperMonkey script to respond

NO_SCRIPT.title: Script not responding
NO_SCRIPT.text: The TamperMonkey script did not respond. Possible causes: TamperMonkey is not installed or disabled; the script is not installed or disabled; user scripts are not allowed in the browser extension settings. Once fixed, just reload the StreamKit window (F5) and the relay will pick it up

OLD_SCRIPT.title: Script outdated
OLD_SCRIPT.text: An incompatible TamperMonkey script version is installed ({version}). Version {minimum} or newer is required. Install the new version from the "Guide" tab and enable the relay again

WAITING_DISCORD.title: Waiting for Discord…
WAITING_DISCORD.text: The script is connected, waiting for voice channel data from the Discord app

DISCORD_SILENT.title: Discord is silent
DISCORD_SILENT.text: The script works, but Discord hasn't sent the channel data. Check whether the Discord app asks to authorize StreamKit (the prompt may be behind other windows) and whether the channel link is correct. Still waiting: as soon as Discord responds, the relay will start working

DISCORD_UNREACHABLE.title: No connection to the Discord app
DISCORD_UNREACHABLE.text: StreamKit can't connect to the Discord app on this computer. Start the Discord desktop app (the browser version won't work) and log in. Still waiting: as soon as Discord starts, the relay will connect by itself

CHANNEL_ERROR.title: Discord didn't return the channel
CHANNEL_ERROR.text: Discord responded with an error to the voice channel request: "{error}". Most likely the channel link is wrong or your Discord account is not a member of this server. Once the link is fixed, the relay will switch by itself

ACTIVE.title: Working
ACTIVE.text: Voice channel events are arriving in FoundryVTT

OVERLAY_CLOSED.title: StreamKit window closed
OVERLAY_CLOSED.text: The StreamKit window was closed and the relay stopped. Press "Reopen" to continue

items.1: The relay can only be launched in a browser. It doesn't work in the FoundryVTT desktop app — the module detects this and tells you
items.2: At least 1 user must have the relay active. Note: even if you host FoundryVTT via the desktop app, you can become the relay yourself by joining the world as another user via a browser

items.1: Relay: a script that runs in the browser and forwards events from a Discord voice channel to FoundryVTT
items.2: Relay player: the player who launched the relay

prep.title: Preparing and activating the relay
prep.intro: All the following steps must be performed by the relay player.

items.1: Install the TamperMonkey extension in your browser and enable it
items.2: After installing, go to your browser's extension settings and configure TamperMonkey depending on your browser:

browsers.other: If you use another browser, or there are no settings with such names, try to find similar settings if the TamperMonkey dashboard still says "Please allow user scripts"

script.title: 2) Installing the script

items.1: Press the button below. A new tab will open, and TamperMonkey will offer to install the script
items.2: Press "Install" (or "Update" if the script is already installed). The old version of the script will be replaced automatically
items.3: Make sure the "Streamkit Speaking Relay" script is enabled in the TamperMonkey dashboard

script.manualTitle: If the button didn't work: manual installation

manual.1: Open the TamperMonkey dashboard and press [+] (create a new script). If the "Streamkit Speaking Relay" script already exists, open it instead of creating a new one
manual.2: Copy the script below, replace ALL text in the editor with it and save:

items.1: Join the FoundryVTT world in the browser where the script is installed and open this window. You can open it from the module settings, a button in the VisualNovelDialogues Theater, or with the game.modules.get("discord-relay").api.openMenu() command
items.2: The GM enters the voice channel link in the "Relay" tab (right-click the channel in Discord → "Copy Link")
items.3: Press "Enable relay". The StreamKit window will open. If Discord asks to authorize StreamKit, allow it
items.4: The "Working" status means everything is fine. If something goes wrong, the "Relay" tab will say what exactly and how to fix it

items.1: You must be in this voice channel to receive the "Started speaking" and "Stopped speaking" events
items.2: Don't close the StreamKit window during the game: closing it stops the relay. Minimizing is fine
items.3: If you reload the FoundryVTT page, the relay will pick up the already open StreamKit window by itself

vnd.title: VisualNovelDialogues integration
vnd.intro: The VisualNovelDialogues module automatically receives relay events. You can configure how VisualNovelDialogues reacts to these events in its settings. By default, on "Started speaking" and "Stopped speaking" events VisualNovelDialogues highlights the character Portraits of the corresponding players. To make it work, follow the instructions below
vnd.subtitle: Preparation

items.1: In the "Relay" tab of this window, assign the corresponding Discord profiles to FoundryVTT users
items.2: In the FoundryVTT player list (usually bottom left), click a player's name and choose "User Configuration". In the window that opens, select the corresponding actor as the player's Character
items.3: Next, open the editor of the Portrait you need, and in the "General" tab link the corresponding actor to this portrait
items.4: Now, when this Portrait is in the Theater, it will be highlighted while the corresponding player is speaking. You can configure the brightness and size of the "highlighted" Portrait in the VisualNovelDialogues settings

help.title: Cheat sheet: what's available in the macro
help.intro: Write the macro as a regular script macro, without Hooks.on. All event data is in a single variable discordEvent (also scope.discordEvent): discordEvent.type, discordEvent.member, etc. Fields match the module's hook arguments. Missing data is null. The ▶ button of a rule runs the macro right now on your side with test data — handy for checking a macro without Discord.

common.member: Discord member: id, nick, name, avatarUrl, mute, deaf (combined: self or moderator), selfMute, serverMute, selfDeaf, serverDeaf, speaking, bot (for member events)
common.foundryUser: Foundry user linked to the member (first one), or null
common.foundryUsers: All Foundry users linked to the member (array)
common.channel: Voice channel: id, guildId, name, topic, userLimit
common.members: All voice channel members (array, like member)
common.rule: The rule that ran the macro
common.speaker: Regular Foundry variables

specific.previous: muted / unmuted / deafened / undeafened / updated: member data before the change
specific.changed: muted / unmuted / deafened / undeafened / updated: only the changed fields, e.g. {mute: true, selfMute: true} or {nick: "Bob"}
specific.reason: speakingStart / speakingStop: null if the event came from Discord; "left", "relayLost" or "snapshot" if the module sent it. channelLoaded: "relayStarted", "channelChanged", "reconnected", "relayChanged" or "clientJoined"
specific.relayUser: relayStarted / relayStopped: the Foundry user who started or stopped the relay
specific.test: Test run (▶ button of a rule): true, otherwise false

macros.testTooltip: Test: run the macro now on your side with test data (no Discord needed). In the macro, discordEvent.test = true

errors.noAccess: the player has no access to the macro. Grant access or check "run even if the player has no access" in the rule
errors.noMacro: No macro selected in the rule
